jobs.description:
_Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant, or outsourcing company.

_Join a team of fintech heroes! 🚀

Performativ is changing the way investment advisors and financial institutions operate. We are building a modern platform for portfolio management, reporting, compliance, trading, and client engagement—replacing fragmented systems, manual workflows, and technology built for another era.

Our customers include wealth managers, asset managers, family offices, and financial institutions across Europe and beyond. We are on an ambitious scaling journey, supported by leading global venture capital investors, and are working to become the platform on which modern wealth management runs.

You can read more about our product at performativ.com.

As our new Senior Software Engineer — Wealth Management Systems 📈

You will help the team solve some of the hardest product and data problems across Performativ’s investment platform.

You will work where financial workflows, product decisions, and technical systems meet: portfolio data, reporting, fees, reconciliation, instruments, transactions, cash, performance, and trading. Your contribution will be turning that complexity into coherent solutions that work across customers rather than becoming a collection of one-off customisations.

This is not a narrowly scoped position. We work as one team, and you should be willing to tackle any important problem within our area.

• You will apply deep experience from wealth management, asset management, private banking, portfolio management, investment operations, trading, custody, or related financial infrastructure to develop sound product and system designs.

• You will investigate problems that cross financial data, calculations, APIs, integrations, operational processes, and production systems—determining their root causes and delivering reliable solutions that others can understand and extend.

• You will bring product thinking to ambiguous requirements, working closely with users and customer-facing colleagues to distinguish reusable platform needs from customer-specific preferences.

• You will use AI agents to produce much of the implementation. We expect you to design the solution, direct agents effectively, challenge their assumptions, review their output, and establish the tests and evidence needed for safe production deployment.

• You will lead when your knowledge makes you the right person to lead, follow through on what you take on, contribute to the work of others, and help teammates succeed.

Experience with performance calculations, valuations, fees, reporting, reconciliation, corporate actions, or portfolio-management systems would be particularly valuable.

We value your passion 🔥

At Performativ, we are builders first. We have ambitious goals and value the time, judgment, and effort people put into their work. You will be trusted to make your mark and help shape how we solve difficult problems.

We do not divide the platform into personal territories. People develop deeper context in different areas, but we solve problems as a team. Autonomy works only when paired with initiative, collaboration, sound judgment, and follow-through.

AI increases our delivery speed, but it does not reduce our engineering standard or our accountability for the result. You must be technically strong enough to recognise weak abstractions, incorrect assumptions, missing edge cases, security problems, and unsafe production behaviour.

This role is based in Copenhagen. We work together primarily from our city-centre office, with flexibility to work from home when it makes sense. You should already be based in Copenhagen or be ready to relocate.

What we can offer you 🌱

• Trust and meaningful responsibility from your first day, with the opportunity to influence both our platform and how we build it.

• Difficult and consequential problems involving financial data, product design, reliability, security, and real operational workflows.

• The opportunity to define an AI-native approach to developing complex financial software and see your work reach customers quickly.

• An ambitious, collaborative team with experience from leading technology companies, consultancies, and financial institutions.

• Strong opportunities for professional development as Performativ grows into a European market leader.

Are you a passionate engineer with experience in product development and quality? Do you want to be part of a cross-functional and global work environment? Do you want to join us to continue to deliver on our ambition creating a world class organization where we thrive are proud and motivated to deliver solutions that improve patient lives?

Then this might be your defining moment. Apply today and join us as our R&D Innovation **New Product Introduction Engineer (Process Development), based in Ballerup, Denmark.

**About The Role

**As part of the Global New Process Introduction organization, you will collaborate closely with R&D designers to influence the product design for manufacturing and assembly (DFM and DFA). You will be responsible for designing, setting up, and validating the process. While working from our Headquarters in Ballerup, Copenhagen area, you will join a global team of colleagues across Denmark, Germany, USA, and Asia, and you will report directly to our NPI Manager, based in Ballerup.

**Key Responsibilities

**In this role, you will be working with a team of project members from cross functions to develop and deliver a new medical product to the market. The role entails varied tasks; however, your main responsibilities will include:

• Lead and/or participate in the development of manufacturing processes and process equipment of new and existing product lines according to current business strategy, quality management system and external regulations

• Process development, validation, optimization, definition of specification and implementation of manufacturing processes

• Utilize Design for Manufacturing and Design for Assembly approaches into process development work

• Responsible for development, specification, technical sourcing/ purchasing and implementation of internal and external manufacturing processes

• Optimize product or process design in cooperation with other functions within R&D

• Process expert for internal and/or external manufacturing processes

• Optimize process or product implementation using appropriate tools

• Be part of an international and local integrated development team and participate in project task where and when required

Traveling might occur in the range of 0-20 days per year.

**Suggested candidate profile

****Skills

**Setting you up for success is one of our cornerstones. To make this path achievable, you likely have experience within healthcare or the medical device industry, particularly in quality processes and design control, either in Engineering or R&D. Experience with risk management for medical devices is also a valuable part of your skill set. Skills and experiences can be earned in many different ways, and we understand that the best fit for the role cannot be prescribed on paper. You are however likely to succeed in this position if you:

• Carry a degree in Mechanical Engineering or other relevant discipline engineering disipline.

• Have a structured approach to your work, whilst remaining open-minded and keep an eye out for driving towards success

• Are a cohesion-minded team player

• Are a self-driven project-oriented individual, with a good analytical toolbox and a ‘’can-do’’-attitude

• Thrive in an international environment that is characterized by cross-functional teamwork

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**Ambu is a company that expands rapidly and has ambitious growth targets. We meet these targets through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international head office with an informal working environment.

We offer great opportunities for personal development. Furthermore, we offer a wide range of professional, social, and financial employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

Just imagine simplifying how complex technology programmes flow across teams, products and functions. Then make it real.

As our Senior Agile Coach, you'll partner with leadership teams and Senior Technical Program Managers to untangle complexity and create value across large-scale programmes and across leadership teams. You'll work across Manufacturing & Supply Chain Technology, identifying where processes, dependencies and ways of working need to change. Using a Lean and continuous improvement mindset, you'll help simplify work, improve organisational effectiveness and build capability for sustainable change.

Redesigned end-to-end workflows across programs, teams and functions to reduce systemic blockers.

The opportunity

Etac is a global leader in innovative assistive devices, dedicated to enabling people to live active and independent lives. Our Export organisation supports a global network of distributors, served by Customer Service teams in Denmark, Sweden and Austria.

Today, those teams operate independently, each with its own processes, systems and service standards. The next step is clear: one integrated Export Customer Service organisation, built to scale. We are now hiring an Export Customer Service Manager to lead that integration and own the result.

You have led this kind of transformation before. You know how to harmonize teams, processes and performance without losing the expertise and engagement that made each team successful.

Your mission

You step into an evolving function with experienced people and clear ambitions. Your mandate: build one coordinated, scalable Export Customer Service organization. Within 12-18 months, you will have delivered:

• 
One team across Denmark, Sweden and Austria, with clear roles, ownership and escalation paths.

• 
Harmonized workflows, consistent service standards, and KPIs that show how we really perform.

• 
A ticketing and case management solution that is live, adopted and used every day, building on the project plan already in place.

The role

As Export CSM, you lead the Export Customer Service teams across three countries, a team of ~10 professionals.

The role is primarily people leadership and change, complemented by hands-on operational involvement. You set the direction, roll up your sleeves when it counts, and make sure every distributor gets a consistent and proactive experience.

You report directly to Nikolaj Takla, Managing Director Export and work closely with Sales, Supply Chain, Logistics and Product Management.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Lead, coach and engage experienced CS professionals across countries and cultures.

• 
Harmonize processes and define clear roles, responsibilities, and ownership.

• 
Introduce service levels, operational KPIs and transparent performance reporting where little exists today.

• 
Drive the implementation and adoption of the new ticketing and case management solution.

• 
Improve workflows, workload distribution and resource planning; cut manual admin and open the door to automation and self-service.

• 
Strengthen the order-to-delivery chain through tight collaboration with Sales, Supply Chain and Logistics.

• 
Balance one standard with the needs of local markets and distributors.

Your profile

You are a builder and can challenge established ways of working and bring people on board with you. You create clarity fast, decide when it is needed, and build trust through consistency rather than control. You read cultures well, because what works in Gedved does not automatically land in Sweden or Austria. And you like pragmatic solutions. Besides, you have:

• 
5+ years in Customer Service, Customer Operations, Sales Support or a comparable function, including people leadership, ideally across locations or countries.

• 
A proven track record of leading Customer Service through transformation: harmonizing, centralizing or integrating teams from a fragmented starting point. This is not your first change journey.

• 
Hands-on experience setting up KPIs, service levels and reporting, and implementing or optimizing Customer Service systems, preferably ticketing or case management.

• 
Solid understanding of order-to-delivery in an international B2B environment. Experience with distributor networks and manufacturing, medical devices, assistive technology or other product-driven industries is a strong plus.

• 
Professional fluency in English. Danish, Swedish or German is an advantage.

What's in it for you

• 
Real impact, real lives. Your work shows up in the daily lives of the people who rely on our products, and in every distributor who gets a faster, clearer answer.

• 
A mandate to build. You own the operating model: structure, KPIs, tooling and ways of working, including taking a planned ticketing and case management solution from draft to daily use

• 
International scope. Daily collaboration across Denmark, Sweden, Austria and our global distributor network.

• 
The package. Competitive salary, solid pension plan and the flexibility of hybrid working, with a regular office presence either in Gedved (Denmark) or Anderstorp (Sweden).

Why Etac

We are a dynamic company on an exciting journey, with job opportunities in several career fields and many parts of the world. As part of our team, you will work in a place that values:

• 
Working with something that helps people

• 
Possibilities to grow within one's role and the organisation

• 
Good work-life balance

• 
Freedom with responsibility

Interested?

Submit your CV by 14-12-2026 at the latest. If you would like to hear more about the position, please contact Christa Buss, TA Consultant via email at extchbu@etac.com].

Etac is committed to building diverse teams. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and life experiences.

About Etac

Etac is a world-leading developer of innovative assistive devices and patient handling equipment. Since 1973, we have been committed to improving quality of life for the individual, family members and caregivers.

Through our specialised product brands, we offer state-of-the-art solutions for a wide range of daily needs and care settings, for people at all stages of life. Headquartered in Sweden, Etac is a global company with around 1 500 employees, sales in over 80 countries and a revenue of approximately EUR 500 million.

Copenhagen / Brøndby, Denmark | HX Product Design, 100% dedicated to a new product.

Make an impact with us

Help shape a new product at Milestone Systems, where what you do matters and people are at the heart of everything we do. You will bring curiosity and continuous learning to an environment grounded in integrity, collaboration and strong relationships.

Help decide what our new product becomes. As a founding product designer, fully dedicated to the initiative, you will work directly with customers and a small Product and Engineering team. Together, you will discover what matters, build working experiments and turn promising ideas into well-crafted experiences.

About the role

We have an early thesis; the customer problems, product scope and workflows are still open. You will help define the product itself, starting with empathy for customers to discover opportunities and frame problems before requirements exist. With Product and Engineering, you will make assumptions explicit, create hypotheses and test them with customers to decide where to invest next.

You will work alongside Product and Engineering from discovery through delivery, building and learning together rather than through sequential handoffs. Together, you will agree ownership and decision rights, so your responsibilities and autonomy are clear. You will report to Damion Bailey, the Head of Product Design.

What you will do

• 
Discover problems worth solving. Personally interview and observe operators, administrators and purchase or adoption stakeholders, focusing on customers facing active problems or real purchase/adoption decisions. Use what you learn to establish which problems merit investment and shape product direction with Product and Engineering.

• 
Build to learn. Independently create functional, code-based experiments using AI-assisted tools, real data and available platform capabilities. Agree learning questions and evidence thresholds, critically review AI output and decide what to pursue, change or stop.

• 
Design and test human + AI interactions. Explore new modalities and interaction patterns that make intelligent systems understandable, balancing automation, transparency, attention and human oversight and control.

• 
Turn learning into customer value. Take validated opportunities toward customer-used pilots and shipped capabilities with Product and Engineering, agreeing feasible milestones and making trade-offs explicit.

• 
Craft experiences that last. Bring interaction design, accessibility and visual detail to production. Let principles and reusable patterns emerge from learning, creating coherence across the initiative and wider Milestone ecosystem.

What success looks like

• 
First weeks: Meet customers directly and begin timeboxed experiments. Agree what each experiment needs to teach you, what evidence will be sufficient to make a decision and when that decision will be made.

• 
Within 60–90 days: Show how customer observations and experiments have changed product decisions and the roadmap.

• 
As opportunities mature: Move validated ideas toward customer-used pilots and shipped capabilities, recording adoption, operational value and remaining uncertainty.

• 
What matters: Reduced uncertainty and validated customer value—not prototype volume or polish alone.

What you bring

Your work matters more than your credentials. No specific degree is required. We look for portfolio evidence and shipped outcomes across four core areas: customer-grounded discovery, independent AI-native building, zero-to-one product judgment and end-to-end design craft. Alongside these, we look for the collaboration, English-language and mobility requirements described under Working together.

• 
Customer-grounded discovery. You have personally interviewed and observed customers, identified opportunities and designed experiments that changed product direction.

• 
Functional, code-based prototyping. You can independently build working prototypes with AI-assisted tools, critically assess the tools’ output and collaborate with engineers at implementation depth. This is what we mean by independent AI-native building.

• 
Zero-to-one product judgment. You have repeatedly helped small, autonomous teams turn uncertain needs into live pilots, shipped capabilities or real adoption decisions. You can explain your contribution, trade-offs and decisions to pursue, change or stop.

• 
End-to-end design craft. You combine interaction design, accessibility, visual craft and systems thinking to make complex, intelligent systems intuitive and trustworthy, with appropriate transparency and human control.

• 
Working together. You collaborate confidently across disciplines, conduct research and communicate in professional English, and are willing to co-locate with the founding team in Copenhagen and travel for customer or partner testing during critical phases.

OPTIONAL (helpful, not required): experience with AI products, enterprise or operational workflows, platform ecosystems, video/security technology, or semiotics and non-verbal communication.

Why this opportunity

You will have direct customer access and close partnership with product and engineering decision-makers. This gives you the opportunity to combine customer discovery, AI-native building and design craft, with learning that helps shape the initiative and influence the next generation of Milestone products.

How you can grow

• 
Deepen your expertise in zero-to-one product creation, AI-native design and product strategy through hands-on founding-team work.

• 
Explore potential development paths toward principal-level experience design or broader product design leadership.

Ready to make an impact?

Excited by the chance to shape what comes next? We would love to see how you think, learn and build.

Apply with your CV and portfolio in English. In your portfolio examples, explain your personal contribution, the customer evidence and the key trade-offs. Show the path from discovery and working experiments to a pilot, shipped capability or adoption decision. An example where evidence led you to stop or substantially redirect an idea is also welcome.

Milestone Systems is a leading provider of data-driven video technology software. Our portfolio includes XProtect video management software, Arcules video surveillance as a service and BriefCam analytics. We amplify what organizations of any size can see, do and achieve with video.

Help us evolve the technical foundation for digital manufacturing at VELUX. As IIoT Platform Technical Lead, you will lead the technical direction of our shared IIoT platform while taking part in engineering. You will enable development teams to build manufacturing applications through reliable connectivity, standardised shop floor data and reusable platform services.

Meet your future team

You will join the Industrial IoT Platform Team, part of IT & Digital Enablement. The team develops and maintains the shared IIoT platform that supports manufacturing applications through connectivity, data and reusable technical capabilities.

As IIoT Platform Technical Lead, you will provide day-to-day technical leadership across the engineering group. Working closely with senior IIoT platform engineers, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders, you will coordinate decisions, coach engineers and help move delivery forward. The role has no formal people-management responsibility.

What We Offer

This role combines contributing to the shared IIoT platform’s technical direction with direct engineering work. You will lead day-to-day technical direction and engineering execution, contributing to design, development, testing, reviews and complex problem-solving. You will turn product priorities into a coherent platform roadmap, engineering practices and clear guardrails.

You will balance a clear technical direction with close collaboration, involving the team in technical decisions and finding practical compromises that support both platform integrity and delivery needs.

The goal in this role means a clear and maintained platform roadmap, faster onboarding and greater reuse, improved visibility of platform health, and well-defined ownership between shared platform capabilities and domain-specific application logic.

More specifically your tasks will be to:

• Own and maintain the IIoT platform technical roadmap, including runtime, frameworks, connectivity components, data contracts, developer tooling, observability and lifecycle enablers. Provide estimates, sequencing, dependency and risk input and coordinate with dependent product teams.

• Coordinate technical planning, reviews and coaching across the platform engineering group, aligning key design decisions with senior IIoT platform engineers. Act as the first technical escalation point. Guide external engineering contributions so standards, knowledge and lifecycle accountability remain within the team. Escalate material architecture and cross-platform decisions through the appropriate technical governance.

• Establish and evolve engineering guardrails, reference patterns and clear development paths. Maintain the boundary between shared platform mechanisms and domain-specific application logic. Own technical data-quality controls at the platform boundary.

• Contribute hands-on to platform services and reusable components through design, development, testing and improvement. Focus your direct contribution where technical depth, complex problem-solving or delivery needs require it.

• Support platform observability, technical investigations and follow-through on incidents, problems and improvement actions in collaboration with the Operations Manager.

• Manage platform lifecycle health, including security, patching, vulnerability remediation, upgrades, documentation, supportability, and technical debt.

The role can be based in Skjern, Østbirk, Kolding or Hørsholm. Regular on-site presence in Skjern and at manufacturing locations in Denmark is required, along with occasional international travel. When tasks and projects allow, you may work from home up to two days per week.

What You Will Bring Into The Organization

You bring 7+ years of relevant experience in software, platform or integration engineering, including technical leadership in an industrial IT/OT or digital manufacturing environment. You understand both manufacturing-domain needs and Unified Namespace. You use that understanding to make technical choices that work for platform users and the engineering team.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Have direct experience building C#/.NET services and APIs. Your experience also includes event-driven or decoupled architectures, Unified Namespace, containerised deployment and modern DevOps practices.

• Bring practical knowledge across industrial connectivity and edge technologies, including MQTT, edge runtimes and container orchestration. You also understand industrial data contracts, observability or SRE practices, and OT cyber security.

• Can translate product priorities into an actionable platform roadmap, technical guardrails and engineering practices.

• Can make practical technical design decisions while involving engineers and relevant stakeholders in finding workable solutions.

• Use effective coaching, facilitation, collaboration and communication skills across engineers, product roles, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders.

• Apply a platform mindset focused on reuse, self-service, consumer enablement, operational excellence and long-term maintainability.

Ready to apply?

Learn more about the VELUX Group online at www.velux.com where you can read more about working at our company and what to expect of our recruitment process.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV as soon as possible. We are conducting interviews on an ongoing basis until we have the right match.

All inquiries will be treated confidentially.

In the VELUX Group, we offer you a world of opportunities and the chance to create a bright future. From the forefront of the roof window category, we enable those who live, work and play under the roof transform their spaces and live a healthier everyday life with more daylight and fresh air.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor in Power System Flexibility and Energy Markets
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a full-time position as Associate Professor in Power System Flexibility and Energy Markets is open for appointment from April 2027 or soon thereafter

Your work tasks
You will join the Intelligent Energy Systems and Flexible Markets (iGRIDS) research group in the Section for Electric Power Systems and Microgrids at AAU Energy, Aalborg University. You will actively contribute to the group’s collaborative research, teaching, and broader academic activities.

Your research will address modelling, optimisation and intelligent management of power and integrated energy systems, with emphasis on electricity markets, demand flexibility, uncertainty-aware scheduling and active distribution networks. You will develop computational and data-driven approaches for flexibility across sectors, including power–heat and power–mobility applications.

You will develop and lead research projects, secure external funding and collaborate with academic, industrial and public-sector partners. You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s, master’s and PhD levels and support AAU’s problem-based learning (PBL) environment. It is also expected that you will be able to undertake teaching in Danish within the first few years of employment.

Your competencies
Applicants should have Associate Professor-level qualifications in electrical power engineering, energy systems or a related field, with a documented record of original research and teaching. Relevant competencies include:

• Energy systems and markets: Expertise in modelling, optimisation, and control of integrated energy systems, including energy hubs, sector coupling, electricity markets, energy economics, demand response, flexibility aggregation, and uncertainty-aware scheduling.
• Grid integration: Experience in integrating renewable energy, storage, and flexible demand into active distribution networks, addressing voltage regulation, congestion management, grid stability, and coordinated flexibility services.
• Research excellence and leadership: Strong publication record and demonstrated ability to develop research directions, secure competitive funding, and lead national and international collaborative projects, particularly EU-funded initiatives.
• Teaching and collaboration: Documented experience in university teaching at bachelor's, master's and doctoral levels. Experience in teaching within Flexible Master's Programmes, particularly for industry professionals, is considered an advantage. Ability to contribute to Problem-Based Learning (PBL), communicate effectively in English and collaborate constructively with students, colleagues and external partners.
• Additional strengths: Experience in experimental validation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and industry-oriented research or teaching is advantageous.
Who we are
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real-world energy challenges.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

Qualification requirements
Appointment as an associate professor requires research and teaching qualifications at the level that can be achieved through the satisfactory completion of a period of employment as an assistant professor but may also be obtained in other ways.  

It is a precondition that applicants have documented research at an international standard. In addition, applicants are assumed to have received supervision and pedagogical skills development and to have obtained a positive written assessment of their teaching qualifications.

How to apply  
Your application must include the following: 

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position 
• Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma) 
• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of ten publications. 
• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see The Faculty of Engineering and Science. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this   
• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc. 
• Additional qualifications in relation to the position 
• References/recommendations 
You can read more about the requirements for your application here.    

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.  

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. The successful applicant is expected, with support from the university, to acquire Danish language skills over time and to be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 2–5 years of employment, including grading and supervising students, at a level corresponding to the teaching undertaken.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? 
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.     

Further information 
Read more about our recruitment process here  

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.  

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. 

Salary and terms of employment  
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Associate professor.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor of Human Nutrition and Nutrient Specific Appetite at the Department of Biomedical Sciences
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Human Nutrition and Nutrient Specific Appetite at the Department of Biomedical Sciences

  Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

  We are looking for a dynamic assistant professor in human nutrition and endocrine regulation of appetite to commence March 1st, 2027 or thereafter.

  The position is linked to the five-year research programme "Hormones from human liver that control appetite", led by Associate Professor Matthew Gillum. You will take a leading role in the human nutrition components of the programme while developing your independent research profile.

  Information on the department can be found at: https://bmi.ku.dk/english/

  Our research

  The Gillum group seeks the endocrine and physiological mechanisms that regulate appetite, food choice and nutrient-specific satiety. Our aim is to understand how signals arising from nutrient metabolism influence eating behaviour and contribute to obesity and cardiometabolic disease.

  The research programme investigates whether the liver releases nutrient-responsive circulating signals that influence appetite for specific nutrients. It combines controlled human nutrient challenges, large-scale plasma proteomics, targeted biomarker analyses and human genetic evidence with mechanistic studies in experimental models. The programme also includes human intervention studies of FGF21 and its effects on sweet preference, food choice and alcohol-related reward based on prior group research.

  We work across human nutrition, endocrinology and experimental physiology, with close clinical and academic collaborations. We value teamwork, open scientific discussion and a supportive environment for developing independent research.

  Your job

  Working closely with the team, you will design, coordinate and analyse human meal and nutrient-challenge studies. You will characterise dietary intake, food preferences and appetite-related outcomes and integrate these with hormonal, proteomic, biomarker and genetic data to identify candidate endocrine signals.

  You will also contribute to human hormone intervention studies, including protocol development, analysis plans and interpretation of findings, and collaborate with colleagues who undertake functional and mechanistic studies. The position provides scope to develop independent projects at the interface of human nutrition and physiology of appetite and metabolic health and to contribute to external funding applications.

  The assistant professor's responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication and academic dissemination duties. 	
• Research-based teaching, examinations and student supervision within relevant biomedical and health science programmes. 	
• Sharing knowledge with society. 	
• Participation in the formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors, taking prior equivalent qualifications into account.   Profile

  Five overall criteria apply for assistant professor appointments at the University of Copenhagen: research, teaching, innovation and societal impact, organisational contribution, and leadership. These criteria provide the framework for the overall assessment of applicants, together with the specific requirements below. Find information about each criterion here: UCPH criteria for recognising merit.

  We are looking for a scientist with a strong interest in how diet and endocrine signals interact to influence appetite and metabolic health, and with the following skills and experience:

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• You have a PhD in nutrition, nutritional epidemiology, physiology, biomedical sciences or a closely related discipline. 	
• You have postdoctoral research experience in human nutrition or metabolism, supported by relevant peer-reviewed scientific publications. 	
• You have experience in the design, conduct or analysis of human nutritional studies, such as controlled meal studies, dietary interventions or epidemiological studies. 	
• You have strong quantitative skills and experience analysing human data on dietary exposures, metabolic traits or nutritional biomarkers. 	
• You have research experience with nutritional biomarkers, omics approaches or genetic epidemiology. 	
• You have experience in university teaching or student supervision and a commitment to further pedagogical development. 	
• You can work independently, coordinate research activities and collaborate constructively across disciplines. 	
• You have excellent written and spoken English and clear scientific communication skills as well as fluency in a Scandinavian language.    Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Research that bridges nutritional epidemiology and experimental human physiology. 	
• Expertise in dietary sugars, food preferences or the endocrine regulation of nutrient intake. 	
• Experience integrating omics or genetic information with nutritional or cardiometabolic phenotypes. 	
• A background in clinical nutrition or experience translating nutritional research into human health contexts. 	
• Success in attracting external research funding and experience communicating research beyond academia. 	
• Formal training in university pedagogy.   Place of employment

  The place of employment is the Gillum group at the Department of Biomedical Sciences, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen, Panum, Blegdamsvej 3B, Copenhagen. We offer stimulating working conditions in a collaborative international research environment, with access to laboratory and human metabolic research infrastructure and opportunities for mentoring and interdisciplinary collaboration.

  Terms of employment

  The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is fixed term for 4 years. The start date is as soon as March 1st 2027 or thereafter.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the applicable agreement between the Danish state and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or another relevant organisation. Depending on qualifications, a salary supplement may be negotiated. 

  Information about relocation, employment and relevant tax arrangements is available from International Staff Mobility: https://ism.ku.dk/

  The position is covered by the applicable Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

  Questions

  For further information, please contact Associate Professor Matthew Gillum at gillum@sund.ku.dk. Information about the Faculty is available at https://sund.ku.dk/.

  Application procedure

  Your application must be submitted in English by clicking "Apply now" in the online advertisement. Your application must include the following documents and attachments, all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (maximum one page). 	
• CV including education, work and research experience, language skills and other skills relevant to the position. 	
• Certified or signed copies of your PhD and master's degree certificates. If the PhD has not yet been completed, a written statement from the supervisor may be provided. 	
• List of publications. 	
• Teaching portfolio or equivalent documentation of teaching, supervision and pedagogical training.   Deadline for applications: 16 December 2026, 23:59 Copenhagen time.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline or applications that do not meet the requirements stated above.

  The further process

  After the application deadline, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an impartial assessor. Once the assessment has been completed, each assessed applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part relating to their own qualifications.

  You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Applicants will be assessed in accordance with the applicable Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  Interviews are expected to take place in week 2, January 2027.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

"We are building Danske Commodities’ new AI platform from the ground up. Our mission is to enable our colleagues to build amazing things on top of a platform they value and trust. Model access, hosting, governance, cost, observability and technology choices are our problems. And frankly, we wouldn’t have it any other way." (Henrik Skaarup Andersen, Head of Core and AI Platform Engineering)

Here’s what the job entails

In the role, your primary function will be to design, build and run the platform layer that AI runs on at Danske Commodities (DC): model access, gateways, identity, hosting, observability, guardrails and agent runtimes. The platform is new. The usage is not. Clause, GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Copilot are already in people’s hands, and part of the job is putting a proper platform underneath what is already running. You will decide where the line goes between a platform concern and an application concern and make the platform side genuinely self-service. You will work directly with the engineers, quants and analysts who use the platform, building the capabilities and experience they need to succeed with their use cases. You will work across the frontier AI stack in production, across multiple vendors, in a company where the decision path is short.

More specifically, your responsibilities include:

• building and running the services that let everyone at DC reach AI models safely. That means the gateway all traffic passes through, how people and systems prove who they are, and which models and which vendors are available at what cost

• making AI capabilities reusable. Instead of every team solving retrieval, tool access, agent hosting and logging on its own, you build it once as a platform offering that the rest of the company builds on top of

• designing the guardrails. Everything is logged and traceable, data stays where it is allowed to be, and legal and compliance requirements are built into the paved path instead of being inspected afterwards

• keeping it reliable and affordable. You define what good looks like in numbers (availability, latency, cost per team), measure it, and act when it drifts rather than when someone complains

• working with the people who use it. Sit with engineers, quants and analysts, understand what blocks them, and turn that into platform capability rather than a ticket queue

Meet your team

You will join our newly formed AI Platform team, and our role is to make AI something people at DC build on rather than something every team wires up independently. We own the platform that makes it possible. We sit in Core Engineering, next to infrastructure engineering, the developer platform, the data platform, security and digital workplace. We serve 250 programmers, 180 of them engineers, plus quants, analysts and operations specialists, and the wider organisation of 600 through AI assistants and hosted agents.

We are a team of three with a large mandate. Decisions get made in the room and shipped the same week. We work across all of Engineering to make things happen. We come with different backgrounds: software engineering and architecture, infrastructure and platform operations. We expect to teach and learn from each other as we go. We build for other people. A capability is not done when it works, it is done when someone else can use it without asking us how. We are opinionated about engineering quality and sceptical of hype. AI changes what we build and how we do it, but not whether we own the quality and verify what we build.

But enough about us… over to you!

As you will be building a new platform in an area that is moving fast, we imagine that you thrive on creating structure where not everything has been defined yet. You are comfortable making decisions, testing what works and taking responsibility for the platform you build. At the same time, you are curious about the people using it and enjoy working directly with users to turn their needs into reusable platform capabilities. We also imagine that you are pragmatic and independent in the way you work. You can distinguish between what belongs in the platform and what belongs in individual applications, and you focus on building solutions for many rather than one.

Furthermore, we imagine that you:

• hold a relevant educational background within Computer Science, Software Engineering or a similar field

• have built and operated a platform that other engineering teams depended on, and been on the hook for keeping it running

• are proficient in software engineering using at least one of .NET, Python, Go or TypeScript, as well as infrastructure as code and Kubernetes

• have worked hands-on with AI infrastructure such as model access, gateways, agents or assistant tooling, or alternatively with machine learning in a platform context

• treat identity, access and security as a design

Please note that prior knowledge of the energy sector is not required for this role.

We’ll take good care of you

At Danske Commodities, we take great care of our people. Joining us means you’ll get a lot of great perks – including social events, cultural experiences, tasty food and benefits to better your health, your life and your future.

Shape your development tailored growth plans, 100+ DC University courses & Harvard Learning access

Global career paths as part of our parent company, Equinor’s 20,000-strong international network

On-site wellness state-of-the-art gym, physio, chiro and massage therapy

HQ in the heart of Aarhus with stunning views, inspiring architecture and close to public transport

…. and much more

**Job Description

**SOUNDBOKS is an innovative tech company and aspiring lifestyle brand. You may have seen us at a music festival, street party, or your friend’s celebration (think: private events combining festival-grade sound with beat-enhancing lights) where special moments are turned into memories. We create the loudest, most durable, and arguably coolest Bluetooth speakers and audio reactive lights on the market.

At SOUNDBOKS, trust and community go hand in hand. People are encouraged to take ownership of their work while knowing they have the support of the team behind them. Voices are heard, ideas are welcomed, and collaboration is what pushes us forward.

This is more than a job - it’s a community where people care about each other, celebrate together, and share the energy of creating something meaningful. Life at SOUNDBOKS is bold, fast, and full of passion - for the product, for the mission, and for showing up as your true self. With 70 team members, this is a place where you can do your best work and truly belong.

ROLE AUDIO ENGINEER

TEAM PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

HOURS FULL TIME

LOCATION COPENHAGEN, DENMARK

START DATE OCTOBER 2026 or ASAP

The Product Development team at SOUNDBOKS is the group responsible for the exciting product journey, taking every step of the development process toward and into mass production. In it’s heartbeat you’ll find collaborative and self-driven team members with a large cross-discipline understanding tied to ownership. They are there to make a difference - for the products, the team and the SOUNDBOKS customers as a whole.

As our Audio Engineer, you'll explore new ways to improve the audio experience across SOUNDBOKS products by combining signal processing, system simulation, and engineering insight. Working closely with the Acoustics, Hardware, and Firmware teams, you'll help shape the technologies behind our next generation of speakers.

Okay, let’s make things a little more concrete. Here’s what we expect your daily life to look like:

**Audio System Development

**

• Develop audio concepts and proof-of-concepts at a system level.

• Explore new approaches to improve audio performance across products.

• Collaborate with the Acoustics, Hardware, and Firmware teams during concept development.

**Signal Processing & Simulation

**

• Perform advanced signal processing simulations with a focus on sound pressure level (SPL), sound quality, and system efficiency.

• Simulate the interaction between acoustics, amplifiers, electronics, and battery performance.

• Evaluate and develop signal processing algorithms to improve overall product audio performance.

**System Performance & Collaboration

**

• Work closely across the entire Product Development team in order to evolve and improve the audio performance across our future product portfolio.

• Apply signal processing methodologies to improve sound pressure, sound quality, and battery performance.

**Job Requirements

****In order to become a success in this role, we believe that your profile should be aligned with the bullets listed below. However, we acknowledge that success can take many forms, so please do apply even if you don’t tick all the boxes.

**

• You hold a BSc or higher in Audio Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Acoustics, or a related engineering field.

• You've designed and simulated audio systems, ideally loudspeakers, and know your way around signal processing for audio.

• You're comfortable using simulations and measurements to test ideas, challenge assumptions, and make better engineering decisions.

• It’ll be considered a plus if you have experience working with loudspeaker design, transducers, enclosure design, or audio electronics.

• You get excited by solving difficult audio problems and finding smarter ways to improve performance.

• You're naturally curious, love experimenting, and enjoy digging into the details until things sound and work better.

• You take ownership of your work and enjoy bouncing ideas around with people who know more than you in their field.

• You're drawn to what SOUNDBOKS is building and are excited to be a part of the journey!

Intrigued? At SOUNDBOKS you’ll find yourself a part of a community. We realize that growth is a process and we don’t expect you to go through it alone. Actually, we guarantee that you won’t have to. We work together in order to work smarter, we inspire each other to be better, and we never forget that every member of the team is responsible for our success.

So, if you’re tired of all of the noise in the job market, we’d love to hear from you. This may be the coolest job you ever have.

jobs.description:
**Location: Copenhagen (please note this job requires onsite presence - remote work not possible)

**Do you want to work hands-on with modern cloud-based technologies, data engineering and AI, while helping turn complex data into solutions that create real business value?

Join us as a Data Engineer to become part of an environment where knowledge is shared, and curiosity is encouraged. And work with tools such as Snowflake, dbt, Claude, Microsoft Azure, SQL and AI as you help develop the data platform that enables actionable insights, intelligent solutions and data-driven applications.

“You’ll get to contribute to solutions for a wide portfolio of customers - without compromising on flexibility and work-life balance. This also allows you to develop your expertise through challenging assignments and collaboration with experienced colleagues,” says Brian Landbo, Manager, SmartX.

**Join an environment built around knowledge, collaboration and growth

**At NTT DATA Business Solutions, we believe that development happens when people learn and solve challenges together. You will become part of our ambitious and agile SmartX team where the pace is high and where we work with modern cloud technologies, data engineering, analytics and AI through our data platform.

**Develop our cloud-based data platform

**As a Data Engineer, you will work closely with analysts, developers and business stakeholders, play a central role in developing our cloud-based data platform, and help transform complex data requirements into robust solutions that deliver real value. You will work across data engineering and AI, while contributing to the foundations that make intelligent and data-driven solutions possible.

**More Specifically, You Will

**

• Develop and maintain data models

• Develop, optimize and quality-assure data pipelines in Snowflake

• Implement transformations, tests and documentation using dbt

• Ensure high data quality through automated testing and validation processes

• Work with Medallion Architecture and modern data warehouse principles

• Support the development of AI-based solutions and data-driven applications

**Experience With The Main Technologies

**You do not need to tick every box. We believe some of the best colleagues grow through curiosity, commitment and a genuine desire to learn. We are looking for a new colleague who enjoys solving complex problems and who is motivated by both technology and the value it can create. You thrive in a collaborative environment where professional dialogue and knowledge sharing are an important part of everyday work. And you enjoy continuously learning and exploring new technologies within data, AI and cloud platforms.

**Finally, We Imagine That You

**

• Have hands-on experience with and a solid understanding of Snowflake as a cloud data warehouse

• Have strong SQL and data modelling skills, including experience with dimensional modelling such as facts, dimensions and star schemas

• Have experience using dbt for data transformation and ETL/ELT processes

• Have worked with data validation, automated testing and documentation

• Have experience with Git and agile development processes

**Ready to build what comes next?

**Then we are happy to hear from you and urge you to hit that “Apply Now“ button.

Apply today and make NTT DATA Business Solutions the place where you grow.

Develop high potential colleagues. Grow leaders. Build succession strength across SGL.

Are you ready to develop high potential people and strengthen leadership across SGL?

As Scan Global Logistics grows and evolves, we want to strengthen how we identify high potential (HiPo), develop leaders and prepare successors for critical roles. We are looking for someone who can turn these priorities into practical programmes and consistent follow-through across countries.

As Global P&C Manager within Development, your primary focus will be talent & HiPo management, to launch our internal development and leadership programmes, succession planning and 1:1 leadership development. You will also support the people aspects of acquisitions, while the Global Chief People & Culture Officer directly leads our people integration.

This is a role with two different rhythms: a planned cycle of HiPo reviews, planning and leadership development, alongside time-sensitive integration support. Development remain your core role and responsibility. During live transactions, you will agree specific support priorities with the Global Chief People & Culture Officer, making trade-offs explicit rather than allowing integration to absorb the role.

What you can expect

• Ownership of practical global HiPo and leadership development programmes, from design and planning to delivery, adoption and follow-up.

• Close collaboration with business leaders and regional and local P&C colleagues to connect development with real business needs.

• A clear core mandate spanning HiPo reviews, development and leadership programmes, succession planning, critical-role mapping and development actions.

• A complementary role in integration: supporting HiPo, retention and leadership alignment under the direct leadership of the Global Chief People & Culture Officer.

In your first year

In your first year, you will help establish a practical HiPo and succession cycle, shape and deliver on our programmes, and ensure that development conversations lead to action. You will also contribute to agreed integration assignments.

Development

• Establish a practical global review cycle with clear criteria, useful preparation and consistent follow-up across regions.

• Facilitate HiPo conversations with leaders and local P&C, translating identified needs into development plans and clear ownership.

• Create practical tools for development conversations, career planning and internal mobility, and support their adoption.

• Track agreed development actions and identify where additional support or decisions are needed.

Programmes and leadership development

• Shape and deliver on our programmes, connecting content with SGL’s business needs, culture and leadership priorities.

• Work with leaders, P&C colleagues and learning partners to organise learning journeys, facilitate sessions and support application in everyday work.

• Evaluate participation, feedback and practical application, and improve programmes based on what leaders and teams need.

Succession and critical-role planning

• Map critical roles and succession coverage with business leaders, identifying readiness gaps and development priorities.

• Facilitate succession discussions and agree concrete actions to strengthen the pipeline for business-critical roles.

• Connect succession plans with leadership development, internal mobility and retention priorities, keeping plans current and actionable.

Integration support

• Support HiPo mapping, critical-role retention and leadership alignment in acquired businesses under the direct leadership of the Global Chief People & Culture Officer.

• Contribute to agreed integration plans, leader communication and onboarding, coordinating with acquired leaders and local P&C colleagues.

• Support agreed people-integration actions, including coordination and harmonisation, alignment with legal, IT and local P&C.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for a hands-on and experienced P&C professional who can build practical programmes, facilitate meaningful conversations with senior leaders and ensure that development plans are implemented—not left in presentations.

• Relevant higher education within HR/P&C, organisational psychology, business, learning and development or a related field.

• At least 5 years of relevant experience in talent management, leadership development, succession planning or organisational development; experience supporting M&A integration is an advantage.

• Proven experience delivering talent reviews, succession planning or leadership development programmes from preparation through implementation and follow-up.

• Strong facilitation and programme management skills, with confidence engaging senior stakeholders and translating discussions into action.

• Ability to connect business priorities with talent pipelines, leadership capability, retention and practical development opportunities.

• Excellent written and spoken English; experience working across countries, cultures and regulatory environments.

What will make you successful

• You create clarity and momentum when information is incomplete and priorities change.

• You handle sensitive people matters with sound judgement, empathy and discretion.

• You balance global consistency with local relevance, and make explicit choices when development priorities and integration support compete.

• You connect strategy with disciplined execution and make sure decisions become action.

• You build trust through practical support and measure progress by stronger succession coverage, implemented development actions and application of learning.

Why join Scan Global Logistics?

At SGL, you will join an international logistics company with an entrepreneurial culture, high ambitions and a strong belief that results are created by people who take responsibility. Our DNA is built on Respect, Integrity, Entrepreneurship & Fun.

You will have the opportunity to shape how SGL develops talent and leaders, strengthens succession and gives colleagues room to grow—while supporting the talent and leadership side of integration.

Interested?

Send your CV and application through the SGL career portal. We review applications on an ongoing basis and will close the process when the right candidate has been found.

For further information, please contact Birgitte Dam, Global Chief People & Culture Officer (+45 7872 5403) or visit www.scangl.com.
